issue.title: test_wipe_does_not_delete_under_the_allocation_lock fails under the full parallel lane, passes in isolation
issue.description:
FOUND BY the sase-xz.land agent while consuming `just check-full` monitor 4fvbspmpxjw5
(landing gate for epic sase-xz, file-aware pager syntax highlighting). Every lint gate,
SASE validation, committed plans, and the whole `just test-cost` full suite passed; the
only failing step was the last one, `just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake`, which
promoted this node with no entry in tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt.

NOT caused by epic sase-xz. All four promoting records are at heads that are not sase-xz
commits (e2ce985dd "fix(bead): give targeted cleanup paths a real owner lookup" x3 and
f28e64334 "refactor(llm-provider): split provider_priority.py under the 500-line cap"),
every one of them on a dirty tree belonging to another workspace, and the agent-name
registry has nothing to do with pager syntax highlighting.

`just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake` is the last gate of `just check-full`, so an
undeclared node here blocks every landing agent that reaches it. This bead is filed so
the node can carry a baseline entry with a named owner.

The test patches `Path.home` to a tmp_path, calls `rebuild_name_registry()`, wraps the
allocation lock so it can tell when the lock is held, replaces
`_wipe_execute.shutil.rmtree` with a tracker, and asserts that
`wipe_agent_names_for_reuse(("beta",))` deletes the agent artifact with zero rmtree calls
made while the lock is held. Root cause is not proven; the natural suspects are the same
process-global registry/memo state that sase-u7 and sase-tt already document
(`tests/test_agent_name_registry_rebuild.py::test_reservation_reads_skip_the_stale_proof_memo`
is an existing baseline entry from that class) and the registry-under-lock contention
described by sase-wy.

task_type_fields.evidence:
Four eligible full-lane records (schema 2, at most 5 failures each) across two unrelated
heads and three distinct change sets, with later full runs passing the node:

1. 20260907T131404Z-f28e64334ade-3440418-full-run.json (head f28e64334, dirty, 3 changed
   files, sole failure).
2. 20260907T141127Z-e2ce985dd5b0-19416-full-run.json (head e2ce985dd, dirty, 2 changed
   files, sole failure).
3. 20260907T143130Z-e2ce985dd5b0-333936-full-run.json (head e2ce985dd, dirty, 5 changed
   files, sole failure).
4. 20260907T135748Z-e2ce985dd5b0-3949628-full-run.json (head e2ce985dd, dirty, 2 changed
   files, 3 failures alongside two unrelated ACE TUI nodes).

Three of the four records have this node as their only failure, so the run was otherwise
green - this is not a broken-suite artifact.

Fail rate: parallel full lane only. Serial isolated rerun on the sase-xz landing tree
passed (`.venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:randomly -q
tests/test_agent_name_registry_lock.py::test_wipe_does_not_delete_under_the_allocation_lock`
-> 1 passed, 0.01s call). The same tree's `just test-cost` full-suite lane also passed
the node. No serial reproduction of the failure.
